Subject: Recap: Migration compatibility discovery + next tests (OpenAI-compatible API)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action plan for the evaluation.

Call notes (high level):
- Primary goal: migrate FinCo's customer-facing assistant from HyperscalerX to an OpenAI-compatible inference API while keeping latency and quality at or above current levels.
- Key concerns raised: streaming latency, function/tool calling parity, embeddings compatibility (semantic recall), tokenization/prompt deltas, and audit/logging for compliance.
- Success criteria: no >2x increase in median tail latency, embedding cosine similarity drop < 2% on baseline eval set, preservation of function-calling behavior for top 10 call patterns.

Proposed test plan (short):
1) API parity smoke test (this week): Rafael will run an OpenAI-compatible request/response sanity suite against example prompts you provided — check streaming, role/name tokens, and function calling. (attachment: redwood-openai-compat-test.sh)
2) Prompt-diff eval (next 3 days): run ~200 prompts from your production set and produce prompt_diff_examples.json with qualitative/regression flags.
3) Perf baseline vs HyperscalerX (1-2 days): 1k requests at representative concurrency to compare p50/p95/p99 cost and latency.
4) Embedding regression check: run embedding subsets and compute cosine similarity against current vectors.

Open questions for you:
- Which of the above is highest priority? (API parity vs embeddings vs perf)
- Can you confirm a test account/keys and an ETA for procurement to sign the evaluation SOW?
- Do you want us to include dedicated capacity sizing for the perf run or use shared hosted endpoints?

Next steps we propose immediately: Rafael to run the compatibility smoke tests (1) — Rafael, we'll need the sample prompts and an external test key when Alice confirms. Alice — are you available for a 30-min tech run on Monday or Tuesday?

I've attached a short migration-plan.pdf that outlines the scripts, expected artifacts, and acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

—Marissa

Hi Alice / Marissa — quick technical notes ahead of the Monday run. Short answers first: yes, Redwood supports streaming + function calling in the same request; we stream event messages with function call chunks and provide final function call payload at the end.

Compatibility notes and what I'll run for the smoke tests:
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions (same param shapes as OpenAI: model, messages, functions, function_call, stream)
- Authentication: Bearer <test-key> — we'll use the read-only key you provide for the smoke tests.
- SDK swap: our open-source SDK mirrors the OpenAI client surface. Example curl (non-streaming):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-3.5-compat","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"${PROMPT}"}]}'

- Streaming: we emit chunked SSE events; function_call chunks are labeled with event.type = "function_call"; the client should accumulate until event.type = "function_call_finish" to reconstruct the full payload. This is what we'll validate.
- Tokenization diffs: our tokenizer is BPE-compatible with the common OpenAI vocab for the 3.5/4-series family; small prompt deltas can occur if you rely on byte-level offsets. We'll provide prompt_diff_examples.json with flagged diffs.
- Embeddings: model name rwd-emb-001 — vector length and transform match common formats; we'll run cosine similarity and return a regression report.

Recommended smoke tests I'll run Monday (deliverables in repo root):
- smoke-results/{timestamp}/api-parity.log  (basic requests + function-call streaming)
- smoke-results/{timestamp}/prompt_diff_examples.json  (sample prompts with delta notes)
- smoke-results/{timestamp}/embedding_regression.csv  (cosine similarity stats)
- perf-baseline/{timestamp}/latency_summary.json (if we run perf)

I've attached a simple script (redwood-openai-compat-test.sh) you can run locally; it exercises chat+stream, function_call, and embeddings. Rafael will run it from our side as well and push results to the shared Drive link.

Notes for procurement: the perf run estimate (shared hosted endpoints) is ~2 compute-hours plus small storage for logs; if you want dedicated capacity, I'll include a sizing proposal after we see the perf numbers.

—Rafael
